$comment: XR Phase 2 · T7 — the module size waiver register.
Constitution Art. V.3: 'No module exceeds a defined size/complexity threshold
WITHOUT AN OWNED PLAN TO SPLIT.' The Article permits an over-threshold module
when there is an owner and a plan; it does not require every module to be under
the line on day one. This file IS that owned plan, and scripts/size-gate.ts
· an over-threshold module missing from this file          -> CI FAILS
· a waived module that GROWS beyond its recorded size      -> CI FAILS
· a waiver missing owner / reason / plan / ISO review date -> CI FAILS
· a waiver for a module now under threshold (stale entry)  -> CI FAILS
So a waiver is permission to be big today, never permission to get bigger, and
the register cannot silently rot into a list of obsolete excuses.
Phase 2 split two modules outright: daemon/dashboard.ts (3619 -> 48 + 3 modules)
and plugins/loader.ts (1586 -> 89 + 3 modules), and deleted memory/store.ts and
workflow/engine.ts from the top-level tree via the T5/T6 retirements.

waivers.reason: A single exported string constant containing the Control Center's browser application. It is DATA to the daemon, never executed server-side, and has zero branching or imports, so LOC does not represent server-side complexity. Phase 4 · T5 appended the CSP-safe action dispatcher (allowlist parser) and act() helper; the file remains a single exported string constant (data, not server-side logic). Phase 8 · T3/T1 appended the keyboard/a11y behavior (aria-current state machine, dialog focus trap/return, Enter/Space activation bridge, tool-card accordion fix) and the versioned-API v1() rewrite (+61 lines, still declarative browser data). Phase 8 · T4 appended the progressive-disclosure nav (Start-here area, collapsible persisted areas), honest readiness banner, undo button, and standardized capability badges (+193 lines, still declarative browser data).
waivers.plan: Phase 3 replaces the inline string with real client modules served as static assets; the split is blocked on the asset-pipeline decision, not on this file.

waivers.reason: The single-writer WorkspaceStore is the Phase-1 durability invariant (ADR-0001). It owns the baseline schema for every table plus the audit hash chain; splitting the connection owner risks re-introducing the multi-writer defect Phase 1 closed.
waivers.plan: Extract the per-domain table DDL into schema modules that the store composes, leaving connection + WriteGate ownership intact. Deferred to Phase 3 so it lands with the durability-quality work rather than mid-consolidation.

waivers.reason: The HTML shell of the Control Center: one template literal with placeholder tokens. Same reasoning as client-script.ts — declarative markup, not logic. Phase 4 · T5 converted inline handlers/styles to data-xr-action + utility classes (size-neutral; +split plan unchanged). Phase 8 · T3 made the shell WCAG-2.2-AA conformant (buttons not href-less anchors, landmarks, labels, dialog semantics) — net -22 lines.
waivers.plan: Split per view (health / chat / audit / settings) alongside the Phase-3 asset pipeline.

waivers.reason: The interactive Shell controller: state machine, key handling, slash commands and palette. Phase 2 already reduced it by routing execution through the envelope.
waivers.plan: Extract slash-command handling and the palette into interfaces/shell/commands.ts and palette.ts. Deferred: the Shell is the surface most exposed to Phase-3 UX work and splitting it twice would be churn.

waivers.reason: ExecutionService is the durable-execution authority consolidated in T6 (records, leases, checkpoints, recovery). Phase 4 · T1 extended trustPlacementToExecution for the lattice placements (gvisor/firecracker map to container-class). Phase 8 · T2 wrapped execute() in an OpenTelemetry envelope span (executeInner split; +34 lines, observability wiring only, no new orchestration logic).
waivers.plan: Extract lease management and recovery orchestration into collaborators behind the existing ExecutionService facade. Deferred to Phase 3 where durability quality is the phase theme.

waivers.reason: The memory engine, relocated under context/ by the T5 retirement. It still serves the legacy user_memory table because the migration is lossless and reversible — deleting the source would break the documented downgrade path.
waivers.plan: Shrinks naturally as ContextService takes over reads; the file is removed when the legacy table is dropped (no earlier than 8.0.0, per ADR-0006).

waivers.reason: Type declarations only — no runtime code. LOC here is schema surface, not complexity.
waivers.plan: Split per bounded context (identity / recovery / certification) when the enterprise module next changes materially.

waivers.reason: The DAG engine relocated under execution/ by the T6 retirement. It keeps delegating agent work through the injected WorkflowAgentRunner (Phase 0 · T3).
waivers.plan: Extract node executors into execution/workflow/executors/* behind the current engine interface. Deferred to Phase 3.

waivers.reason: Prompt-injection detection and response. Splitting a security-critical detector mid-consolidation risks a coverage gap; the canonical policy gate (guard.ts) is already separate.
waivers.plan: Extract the detector rule set into security/shield-rules.ts, leaving orchestration in shield.ts. Scheduled with the Phase-4 isolation work that also touches this module.

waivers.reason: The canonical context store's persistence layer: five tables plus their queries, and the T5 migration target.
waivers.plan: Phase 6 appended the lifecycle columns/migration, the conflict-resolutions table and the ops undo ledger (+329 lines). Split per aggregate (items / provenance / packages / summaries / ops) once the memory retirement window closes; the ops+resolutions half is a clean extraction seam.

waivers.reason: A single Zod schema plus load/save. It is one cohesive declaration and the single source of truth for configuration shape; splitting the schema would create multiple partial truths. Phase 4 · T1/T4 added security.hardened + security.allowedHosts schema fields and the env-override helper. Phase 5 added the additive difficultyRouting/breaker/retry intelligencePlane fields and migration 17→18 (+47 lines, schema-only). Phase 8 · T2 added the additive telemetry subtree (opt-in, structural-by-default, redacted, local-first; +30 lines, schema-only, no migration needed — defaults fill). Launch S-1 · F3 added the additive envOverrides/envOverridesLocked fields and applyEnvOverrides (explicit env-var -> config-path contract with proto-pollution guards and schema re-validation; +83 lines, no migration needed - defaults fill), pinned by test/config/env-overrides.test.ts.
waivers.plan: Split into per-section schema modules composed into one exported ConfigSchema, preserving the single export.

waivers.reason: CLI command surface: a long flat dispatch over enterprise subcommands, low branching depth per handler.
waivers.plan: Split per subcommand group when the enterprise CLI next changes.

waivers.reason: Type declarations only — the ContextItem model with consent, trust, provenance and freshness. No runtime code.
waivers.plan: Stable by design; Phase 6 added the lifecycle-stage enum, lifecycle-aware tier resolution (defaultTierForItem) and integrity/channel explanation fields (+67 lines) — declarations only. Revisit only if the context model gains a new aggregate.

waivers.reason: Playwright driver: one adapter over a broad third-party API surface.
waivers.plan: Split per operation family (navigation / input / extraction) if it exceeds 1000 lines.

waivers.reason: Type declarations plus pure state-transition tables for the workflow model. No I/O.
waivers.plan: Stable by design; the state machine already lives in its own module.

waivers.reason: The declarative CLI command catalogue — data, not behaviour. It is the contract the L6 compatibility suite verifies.
waivers.plan: Split per command group if it exceeds 1000 lines.
